A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same retrieval/copying study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical arguments, and appendices are readable and matchable despite v3's expanded title and additional material.

before.justification: v1 reports original prompting, training-from-scratch, fine-tuning, and attention-head intervention experiments, including naturalistic copying and Git-history tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds word-level evaluations, Qwen3 results, and longer-context copying results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The task operations, masked-loss GPT-2 fine-tuning, positional offsets, and two-pass induction/anti-induction interventions are retained. Appendix E explains activation handling and reversed target indices more explicitly without establishing a changed intervention procedure.

E1.justification: v3 substantially extends input coverage with English-word versions of all ten retrieval/copying tasks, evaluated up to length 300, and Lorem Ipsum copying at 2,000, 3,000, and 5,000 tokens. v1's corresponding synthetic tasks use characters, and its Lorem Ipsum evaluation centers on approximately 500 tokens. The original task definitions and Git-history scenario remain.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 adds Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-14B, including thinking variants, to the capability comparisons alongside the retained Llama-3/Qwen2.5 models. Section 4.3 also newly reports the pretrained GPT-2 control's effectively zero performance before fine-tuning; the original head-removal comparison conditions remain.

E3.justification: The main character evaluation changes from ASCII inputs capped at length 50 to a vocabulary including diacritics and lengths through 100. Corresponding Figures 10–12 change from best-prompt results in v1 to averages across prompt variants in v3, materially changing the reporting protocol. Added word-level and long-paragraph experiments introduce further length settings, while the scratch-training and fine-tuning protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether the biases survive replacing synthetic characters with words, using Qwen3 thinking variants, and increasing Lorem Ipsum length tenfold. These directly probe vocabulary dependence, reasoning-model robustness, and error behavior at longer contexts. The existing causal head ablations and layer-localization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three-seed averages and fine-tuning seed lists remain, but Figure 3 no longer displays the prompt-sensitivity error bars present in v1. The new long-context experiment explicitly uses one seed, rather than reducing runs for an existing experiment. This conflicts with the added checklist's statement that every experiment uses at least three seeds.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive length-specific, word-level, and Qwen3 results. For example, its new Table 8 reports Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ambiguous-bigram success of 0.75, 0.43, and 0.19 at 2k, 3k, and 5k tokens, with unambiguous success remaining 0.99. The revised in-context scores involve changed inputs and aggregation, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains; the original fine-tuning and mechanistic result graphics are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.1 corrects Corollary 10 from stating that word-order reversal is expressible in C-RASP[pos] to stating that it is not expressible. This resolves a contradiction with the already-present inexpressibility proof and intuition. The central theorems, constructions, and proof arguments otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: pretraining favors induction over anti-induction, targeted fine-tuning can remove directional asymmetry, and architectural length-generalization limitations persist. Naming these patterns Directional Bias and Uniqueness Bias and adding supporting experiments do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3 more explicitly qualifies the theoretical guarantee as requiring idealized training with all data through a maximum length and exact regularized-loss minimization, distinguishing it from empirical SGD/RoPE evidence. Appendix C.3 adds an inner-lexicon rationale for interpreting word-level tasks. The principal mechanistic interpretation and Section 5 limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies exact character and word vocabularies and clearer path-patching instructions, including backward-copy target indexing. Appendix F adds hardware allocations for 4B/14B models and revises estimated reproduction compute from 1,500 to 2,500 H100 GPU-hours. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameter tables and the repository link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds model-report citations, Kaplan et al. (2025) on the inner lexicon, and references supporting question-answering/RAG motivation. It removes Weiss et al. (2021) alongside the shortened RASP background. These are limited updates within the same positioning around length generalization and induction circuits.

P1.justification: v3 expands the title, changes author ordering, consistently names the two biases, refines explanatory passages, and reorganizes Appendix C. It also adds acknowledgements, contributions, and a conference checklist. The main section sequence and most existing scientific prose remain recognizable rather than undergoing wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 3 and Figures 10–12 change from aggregate bar charts to multi-panel plots showing accuracy against input length. v3 adds Qwen3 and word-level plots and a long-context results table. Existing circuit, fine-tuning, and mechanistic graphics are retained or relocated, including old Figures 13–14 becoming Figures 25–26.

improvement.justification: The word-level, thinking-model, and longer-context checks provide useful corroboration, while the revised plots expose length effects hidden by v1's aggregate displays. Correcting Corollary 10 and clarifying the theoretical guarantee improve precision. These gains are tempered by removed prompt-sensitivity error bars and the single-seed long-context experiment's inconsistency with the checklist, yielding a limited net improvement.
